question: Calibrate manual improvement (A, alpha ~ U(0.05,0.25)) to the same evidence standard as B, C and D: find 2021+ field or audit measurements of savings from non-technology process fixes (checklists, standard work, queue management) in back-office finance or compliance operations, including realized-versus-planned ratios
conclusion_affected: Which intervention ranks first once every option is held to field evidence; whether C's rank-first probability rises from 0.2-1% to 4-35% (ABD_FIELD)
rationale: When only B and D are cut to realized savings, manual improvement A becomes the modal gross winner in 6-7 of 15 processes because alpha is still a v1 prior. Applying the same realization range to A as well (ABD_FIELD) is what moves C, so A is now the binding uncalibrated parameter

question: Redesign realization: collect 2021+ inspector-general, GAO or NAO audits that compare claimed and verified savings from process redesign or shared-services consolidation (not RPA), to replace the RPA-by-analogy realization range now applied to D
conclusion_affected: D's gross value pool (falls from $3.8m to $2.1m at a large national under BD_FIELD) and the break-even realization at which C overtakes
rationale: The only 2021+ realized-versus-planned audits found are for RPA (HUD OIG 7% of estimate; GSA OIG 9 of 10 bots off estimate). D's realization range is borrowed from them [I]; redesign may realize more or less

question: Choi & Xie (E17) full text: retrieve the Journal of Accounting Research open-access version (CC BY) through a robots-permitted route and extract accountants' intervention rates and error rates by AI confidence-score band
conclusion_affected: Routing parameters h and e for bookkeeping-type processes (P02, P10, P12, P15)
rationale: SSRN abstract page and both Wiley full-text URLs returned HTTP 403 (bot challenge) on 2026-11-19; only the abstract-level 8.5% time reallocation is available. The paper is the only field study of confidence-gated intervention in accounting

question: Escaped-error cost m for compliance processes: build a per-missed-SAR cost range from public 2021+ BSA/AML enforcement orders that state both the penalty and the count of unfiled SARs or missed alerts (FinCEN 2026-03 Bank of America: about 8,900 SARs missed in the lookback; other FinCEN and OCC orders), expressed in handling-time units
conclusion_affected: Routing pool and C's rank under m (routing pool $1.36m at m=1 falls to $44k at m=20 in the routing note); P14 and P01
rationale: m is the one routing parameter with no source. The BofA order is the first retrieved document that pairs a missed-detection count with a penalty, a 5% false-negative tolerance and a staffing response (+750 staff when the threshold was corrected)

question: Fixed costs F_B and F_D against audited bot and project costs: extract per-bot development cost and hours saved from HUD OIG 2021-OE-0007 Appendix A, GSA OIG A210057 and any other 2021+ IG RPA audits, and compare with the model's F_B log-uniform $100k-$500k
conclusion_affected: Net ranking (B's P(net>0)); whether conventional automation clears its fixed cost at community-foundation scale
rationale: HUD OIG reports $489,885 spent on a bot expected to save 100 hours a year and at least nine bots never completed; the recut only changed gross B, not F_B

question: Per-process auto-close share h: replace the single global h with process-specific ranges using the confidence-band evidence (AML alerts 0.20-0.78, document review 0.65-0.80, invoice fields 0.28-0.49 at 5-10% error) and re-run the routing variant
conclusion_affected: Which processes C can win (P07, P11 under A01 ranges)
rationale: The A01 range h ~ U(0.20,0.80) pools evidence from different domains; the upper half comes from a retrospective AML validation and an agency self-report, and is above the E19 range used in the routing note
